study_identification_part.si3_author_journal_year: Wu and Baeken, Biological Psychiatry: Global Open Science, 2023
study_identification_part.si4_title: Sex Determines Anterior Cingulate Cortex Cortical Thickness in the Course of Depression

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The paper clearly states objectives: to examine how ACC cortical thickness differs by sex and across first-episode vs. recurrent MDD, and it explicitly states the use of normative modeling to investigate individual-level variability. This satisfies both criteria: research questions/hypotheses are provided and the purpose of applying normative modeling (to capture individual-level heterogeneity) is described.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text:
"...we contrasted 499 patients with MDD... and 524 healthy control participants using linear mixed-effects models and normative modeling and investigated whether sex differences affected ACC CT and its subregions differently during the course of depressive illness." 
"Finally, to assess the within-group heterogeneity, we also applied neuroanatomical normative modeling to capture individual-level variability in ACC CT..."

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: This study builds a new normative model using data from REST-MetaMDD. Eligibility and quality criteria are specified (DSM-IV MDD for patients; HAMD ≥14; exclusions for poor image quality, small site sample sizes, and missing medication info). Image quality control is described. Final sample sizes and the number of sites are reported.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text:
"...participants were also excluded for the following reasons: 1) poor image quality... 2) coming from a hospital site with both patient... sample sizes < 5; and 3) no information on medication status." 
"Consequently, 499 patients... and 524 HCs... were selected from 9 study sites." 
"Quality controls of all CT images were conducted before further statistical analysis."

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: Covariates (age, sex, education) are explicitly included. Multi-site effects are handled via site-specific random effects in LME and hierarchical Bayesian regression in the normative model.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text:
"...we added sex, age, and education as covariates in the analysis." 
"Hierarchical Bayesian regression analysis was employed to accommodate intersite variation and generate normative models using the covariates of sex, age, and education."

nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.reason: Per guidance, for SECONDARY data (existing datasets), this item is not applicable. The study uses REST-MetaMDD and refers to the original publication for acquisition parameters.

nm5_data_preprocessing.reason: Preprocessing software and steps are clearly described: SPM12 segmentation, ANTs DiReCT for cortical thickness, DARTEL modulation/resampling, and quality control of CT images.
nm5_data_preprocessing.supporting_text: "...segmented into gray matter, white matter, and CSF using the SPM12... Then, CT estimation was... by the DiReCT ... in ANTs... Finally, the resulting CT maps were modulated and resampled... using the DARTEL algorithm... Quality controls of all CT images were conducted..."

nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.reason: For a newly built normative model, the guide expects a partitioning strategy (e.g., CV, hold-out). The paper does not report training/validation/test splits or cross-validation for the normative model; only LME analyses and normative z-score computation are described.
nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: No explicit mention of cross-validation, hold-out test sets, or similar internal validation for the normative model was found in Methods.

nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.reason: No independent external healthy dataset is reported for validating the normative model. Analyses are conducted within the REST-MetaMDD-derived sample.
nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: The Methods and Results sections do not describe application of the normative model to an external healthy cohort.

nm8_normative_modeling_approach.reason: The normative modeling approach is specified: neuroanatomical normative modeling using PCNToolkit v0.18 with hierarchical Bayesian regression to accommodate intersite variation; covariates are sex, age, and education; z-score deviations are computed.
nm8_normative_modeling_approach.supporting_text: "...applied neuroanatomical normative modeling... within the PCNToolkit (version 0.18)... Hierarchical Bayesian regression... to accommodate intersite variation... using the covariates of sex, age, and education. The deviations (z statistics)... were computed..."

nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.reason: The paper does not report quantitative fit/calibration metrics (e.g., R^2, prediction error, coverage) for the normative model. It only states that z-score-based results are similar to raw CT analyses.
nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "Compared to the raw CT values, similar results were observed for (sub)ACC CT z scores that were derived from the normative model..."

nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.reason: No data partitioning strategy (train/validation/test or CV folds) is described for the normative model; therefore, characteristics per partition are not applicable as per guidance.
nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.supporting_text: No partitions for normative modeling are reported in Methods.

cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.supporting_text:
